name: ML structure prediction and neural force fields
summary: Deep networks predict protein structure from sequence and learn machine-learned potentials for MD, replacing explicit physics with learned surrogates trained on data.

name: ML weather emulators
summary: Neural surrogates trained on reanalysis now match or beat numerical weather prediction at medium range at far lower cost, replacing PDE integration with learned dynamics.

name: MD of ion transport in electrolytes
summary: MD, including machine-learned potentials, computes ionic conductivity and diffusion in solid electrolytes and battery materials.

name: MD simulation of protein folding and dynamics
summary: Force-field molecular dynamics, enhanced sampling and specialised hardware are used to simulate folding, binding and conformational change of proteins, connecting folding landscapes to integrated equations of motion.

name: Protein folding as a test case for MD
summary: Folding timescales and force-field accuracy drive MD development (thermostats, enhanced sampling), while MD supplies atomistic folding pathways that test energy-landscape theory.

name: Trajectories on potential energy surfaces
summary: Classical and ab initio MD trajectories sample reactive events, test transition-state theory and recrossing, and give rate constants via rare-event methods.

name: Ab initio MD of surfaces and catalysis
summary: DFT-based MD and kinetic Monte Carlo model adsorption, diffusion and reactions on catalyst surfaces.

name: Monte Carlo simulation of PET and SPECT
summary: Monte Carlo photon transport (GATE, GEANT4) models scatter, attenuation and detector response, used for system design and image correction in emission tomography.

name: Monte Carlo dose calculation
summary: Metropolis-era stochastic sampling of particle transport is the gold standard for dose calculation in photon and proton therapy, tracking showers event by event.

name: Symplectic tracking of beams
summary: Long-term particle tracking in rings uses symplectic integrators to preserve phase-space structure over billions of turns, as in celestial mechanics.

name: Numerical weather and climate models
summary: Weather and climate models discretise the primitive equations with finite-volume, spectral and semi-implicit schemes; numerical stability and conservation properties are central, and chaos limits predictability.

name: Ocean general circulation modelling
summary: Ocean models rely on finite-volume/difference solvers for stratified rotating flow; numerical diffusion and resolution of eddies control simulated heat uptake and AMOC.

name: DMRG for strongly correlated molecules
summary: DMRG, developed for 1D spin chains, was adapted to quantum chemistry as a multireference method for active spaces of transition-metal and other strongly correlated molecules.

name: MCTDH and tensor-train wavepackets
summary: Multilayer MCTDH for quantum nuclear dynamics on potential energy surfaces is a hierarchical tensor decomposition equivalent to tree tensor networks.

name: Fourier transform: k-space MRI and Radon slice
summary: MRI data are samples of the Fourier transform of magnetisation (k-space) and CT sinograms relate to it via the Fourier slice theorem, so image formation is Fourier analysis.

name: Wave equation and Green's functions in seismology
summary: Seismic wavefields are solved as elastic wave equation with Green's functions; source inversion and ambient-noise correlation recover the Green's function between stations.

name: Inverse problems in tomographic reconstruction
summary: CT reconstruction (filtered back-projection, iterative, regularised) is a linear inverse problem solved with Fourier slice theorem, SVD and regularisation.

name: Differential geometry of membranes
summary: Membrane shapes are surfaces whose mean and Gaussian curvature enter the Helfrich bending energy; Gauss–Bonnet makes topology constrain vesicle shape.

name: Noise limits and lock-in detection
summary: Lock-in detection, shot-noise and thermal-noise limits govern SQUIDs, NV magnetometers and atomic sensors alike.

name: Scintillators and photodetectors in PET
summary: Scintillator crystals, SiPMs and fast timing electronics from particle detectors underpin gamma cameras and time-of-flight PET, with noise and timing resolution as the figures of merit.

name: Statistical inference for single-molecule traces
summary: Hidden Markov models, maximum likelihood and Bayesian change-point analysis extract states and rates from noisy FRET and tweezer trajectories.

name: Detection and attribution as inference
summary: Climate detection and attribution applies optimal fingerprinting, regression and Bayesian inference to separate forced signal from internal variability, analogous to discovery claims in particle physics.

name: Point groups and selection rules
summary: Group representations of molecular point groups and SO(3) determine which vibrational, rotational and electronic transitions are allowed in IR, Raman and electronic spectra.

name: Symmetry adaptation in electronic structure
summary: Spin and spatial point-group symmetry classify molecular states and reduce cost of Hartree–Fock, CI and coupled-cluster calculations.

name: Liouville and Courant–Snyder invariants
summary: Hamiltonian phase-space structure gives conserved emittance and Courant–Snyder invariant for linear optics, with symplectic maps constraining beam evolution; damping breaks it.

name: Symmetry breaking in developmental patterning
summary: Turing-type instabilities and polarity establishment in cells resemble symmetry-breaking bifurcations with order parameters and Goldstone-like soft modes in active matter.
breaks: Living systems are driven, non-equilibrium and finite, with no true Goldstone theorem or thermodynamic limit.

name: Scaling laws in cell and membrane mechanics
summary: Dimensional analysis and scaling fix the bending-rigidity length scales, low-Reynolds-number motility and size dependence of cell mechanics.

name: Nondimensional numbers in geophysical flow
summary: Rossby, Ekman, Richardson and Reynolds numbers from Buckingham-π analysis identify the regimes of rotating stratified flow, justifying geostrophic and quasi-geostrophic approximations.

name: Quantum standards realise SI units
summary: Josephson and quantum Hall effects realise volt and ohm via h and e; atomic clocks and atom interferometers tie units to invariants of nature.

name: Action–angle variables and Courant–Snyder invariant
summary: The Courant–Snyder transform is a canonical change to action–angle variables for linear betatron motion. The invariant is the action J and the phase advance is the angle.

name: Beam optics as Hamiltonian flow
summary: Particle motion in accelerators is Hamiltonian, so Liouville's theorem makes emittance conserved. Linear transfer maps are symplectic and Twiss parameters follow from them.
map: M^T J M=J,\;\epsilon=\sqrt{\langle x^2\rangle\langle x'^2\rangle-\langle xx'\rangle^2}

name: Classical trajectories and phase-space transition states
summary: Reaction rates are computed from classical Hamiltonian trajectories on potential energy surfaces, and transition-state theory uses phase-space dividing surfaces and invariant manifolds.
breaks: Tunnelling and non-adiabatic effects need quantum treatment.

name: Hamiltonian treatment of spin dynamics in MRI
summary: Spin motion in a magnetic field maps onto a rotating-frame equation that parallels the rigid-body rotation formalism, which is used in pulse sequence design.
breaks: Relaxation makes the dynamics dissipative, so phase-space volume is not conserved.

name: Fermat principle and seismic ray tracing
summary: Seismic travel-time tomography uses Fermat's principle and Snell's law to trace rays through velocity models, with the ray parameter conserved in a spherical Earth.

name: Fermat's principle in ray-based imaging
summary: Fermat's principle gives ray paths through tissue and in the Earth, used in travel-time and ray-based reconstruction. It underlies delay-and-sum beamforming and sound-speed estimation.

name: Navier–Stokes to geophysical fluid dynamics
summary: Atmospheric dynamics is the Navier–Stokes/Euler system on a rotating, stratified sphere, with the Boussinesq and hydrostatic approximations and geostrophic balance as reductions.

name: Helfrich bending elasticity of membranes
summary: Membrane bending energy is the thin-shell elasticity of plates adapted to fluid bilayers, with curvature energy governing vesicle shapes and buckling-like transitions.
breaks: The bilayer is a 2D fluid with no shear modulus, unlike solid plates.

name: Earth as an elastic body
summary: Seismic waves, free oscillations and mantle stress response use linear elasticity, with viscoelastic extension for postglacial rebound.

name: Elastic moduli and seismic wave speeds
summary: Seismic P and S wave speeds follow from the Lamé constants and density of the elastic wave equation. Tomography inverts them to map Earth's interior.

name: Elastography: tissue stiffness from shear waves
summary: Shear wave elastography measures shear wave speed in tissue to infer the shear modulus, an inverse problem in linear elasticity used to detect tumours and fibrosis.

name: Ocean circulation as rotating viscous flow
summary: Ekman layers, boundary-layer theory and vorticity dynamics explain wind-driven gyres and western boundary intensification (Stommel and Munk).

name: Plateau–Rayleigh and membrane shape instabilities
summary: Surface-tension-driven pearling and tubulation of lipid tubes echo the Plateau–Rayleigh instability, with bending rigidity and membrane tension setting the selected wavelength.
breaks: Membranes have bending elasticity and fixed area, unlike simple liquid jets.

name: Convective instability in the atmosphere
summary: Moist and dry convection and the Rayleigh–Bénard/Lorenz system share a buoyancy-driven instability criterion. Brunt–Väisälä frequency marks stratified stability.

name: Mantle convection and the geodynamo
summary: Rayleigh–Bénard convection with a Rayleigh-number threshold describes mantle convection driving plate tectonics, and rotating convection in the outer core drives the geodynamo.
breaks: Mantle viscosity is strongly temperature-dependent and non-Newtonian, and the core also needs magnetic and rotational effects.

name: Cell mechanics and viscous microhydrodynamics
summary: Vesicle dynamics, cytoplasmic flow and cell crawling combine membrane elasticity with viscous Stokes flow. Dimensionless numbers such as the capillary number control deformation.

name: Stokes flow in cells and membranes
summary: Cell motility, cytoplasmic and membrane flows occur at very low Reynolds number. Membrane hydrodynamics (Saffman–Delbrück) and swimming under time-reversal constraints use Stokes flow.

name: Overdamped dynamics and Stokes drag in tweezers
summary: Optical and magnetic tweezers experiments operate at low Reynolds number, where Stokes drag on beads sets the calibration and fluctuation-dissipation relations.

name: Atmospheric turbulence and cascades
summary: The atmosphere shows a 3D Kolmogorov cascade at small scales and a quasi-2D inverse energy cascade at synoptic scales. Eddy fluxes need closure in models.

name: Rutherford scattering and molecular beam collisions
summary: Classical central-force scattering with impact parameter and deflection function underlies crossed-molecular-beam analysis, including rainbow and glory scattering.

name: Resonances and N-body methods in accelerators
summary: Resonance overlap, secular perturbation theory and symplectic integrators from celestial mechanics are used for accelerator tracking and long-term stability. Space-charge tracking is an N-body problem.

name: Rotating-frame physics of the planet
summary: Earth-system flows are best described in the rotating frame. Coriolis effects shape circulation, ocean gyres and inertial oscillations.

name: Coriolis force and geostrophic balance
summary: The Coriolis force from Earth's rotation balances pressure gradients to give geostrophic wind and drives cyclone rotation and Rossby waves.

name: Rossby waves from the beta effect
summary: The variation of the Coriolis parameter with latitude gives a restoring mechanism for planetary Rossby waves and westward phase propagation.

name: Tipping points as bifurcations
summary: Climate tipping elements (ice-albedo, AMOC) are modelled as saddle-node bifurcations with hysteresis in energy-balance models. Early-warning signals come from critical slowing down.
breaks: Real climate is forced, noisy and non-autonomous, so rate-induced tipping happens without a classical bifurcation.

name: AMOC bistability (Stommel model)
summary: Stommel's two-box model of thermohaline circulation has two stable states joined by saddle-node bifurcations, giving hysteresis and collapse scenarios.
breaks: Box models omit wind-driven and eddy dynamics, so whether the real AMOC is bistable is contested.

name: Chaos limits climate and weather prediction
summary: Sensitivity to initial conditions bounds weather forecasts, motivating ensemble prediction. Climate is a boundary-value problem about statistics of the attractor.

name: Lorenz chaos and weather predictability
summary: Lorenz's truncated convection model gave the first strange attractor. The result sets the finite predictability horizon of weather (~2 weeks), set by Lyapunov growth of errors.

name: KAM tori and dynamic aperture
summary: Nonlinear magnet errors make betatron motion a perturbed Hamiltonian system. Resonance islands, chaotic layers and surviving KAM tori set the dynamic aperture and beam lifetime.

name: Solitons, tsunamis and internal waves
summary: Shallow-water KdV solitons describe tsunamis and ocean internal solitary waves, balancing nonlinear steepening against dispersion.
breaks: Real waves have dissipation, rotation and variable bathymetry, so exact integrability is lost.

name: Reaction–diffusion patterning of cell polarity
summary: Cell polarity and motility waves on membranes (Min proteins, Rho GTPases) are excitable or Turing-type reaction–diffusion patterns.

name: Turing patterns and Kuramoto sync in biology
summary: Developmental patterning follows Turing reaction–diffusion instabilities, and neural and circadian rhythms follow Kuramoto-type phase locking.
breaks: Real gene networks are noisy and finite-sized, and Turing patterns need fine-tuned diffusivity ratios that biology rarely supplies.

name: Molecular vibrations as normal modes
summary: Molecular vibrational spectra are the normal modes of coupled atoms on a potential surface, found by diagonalising the mass-weighted Hessian, as for coupled springs.

name: Earth's free oscillations as normal modes
summary: After large earthquakes the Earth rings in toroidal and spheroidal normal modes. These are the eigenmodes of a continuum coupled-oscillator system and constrain the PREM structure.

name: Cavity resonance and Q factor in RF cavities
summary: Accelerator RF cavities are driven resonators characterised by Q and bandwidth, and superconducting cavities reach Q of 10^10 or more. Their response follows the driven damped oscillator.

name: Larmor precession and resonance in MRI
summary: Nuclear spin in MRI follows classical gyroscopic precession and driven resonance, with Bloch-equation relaxation like a damped driven oscillator (T1, T2).
breaks: Spin is quantum and the Bloch equations are linear only for ensemble magnetisation.

name: Ocean waves, tides and dispersion
summary: Surface gravity waves, internal waves and tides obey dispersion relations for fluid waves. The deep-water relation gives dispersive group and phase speeds.

name: Wave propagation in the Earth
summary: Seismology applies reflection, refraction, impedance and dispersion of mechanical waves to layered media. Surface waves, free oscillations and travel-time inversion probe structure.

name: Acoustics underlying ultrasound imaging
summary: Echography relies on impedance mismatch reflection, attenuation, Doppler shift and beamforming of acoustic waves in tissue. Elastography uses shear wave speed to measure stiffness.

name: Medical acoustics: impedance and Doppler
summary: Ultrasound transducers, tissue attenuation and Doppler blood-flow measurement are applications of acoustic wave theory.

name: Mathieu/Hill equation and strong focusing
summary: Betatron motion in an alternating-gradient lattice obeys Hill's equation, a periodically driven oscillator like Mathieu's. Stability bands match parametric resonance, and alternating focusing resembles Kapitza stabilisation.

name: Gyroscope sensing, classical to atomic
summary: Mechanical gyroscopes sense rotation via angular momentum conservation, and atom-interferometric gyroscopes measure the same Sagnac-type rotation with matter waves at far higher sensitivity.

name: Earth's precession, nutation and inner core
summary: Precession and nutation of Earth's axis depend on its moment of inertia and on core structure, so the free core nutation constrains interior properties.

name: Moment of inertia constrains density profile
summary: Earth's moment of inertia factor (about 0.33) is a global constraint on radial density models such as PREM, showing a centrally condensed structure.

name: Optics and imaging theory in medical imaging
summary: Transfer functions, resolution limits and Fourier-based image formation from optics carry over to radiography, CT and MRI image-quality analysis.

name: Coherence of X-ray sources
summary: Diffraction-limited storage rings and FELs are characterized by transverse and longitudinal coherence, with van Cittert–Zernike propagation and emittance matching the diffraction limit $\lambda/4\pi$.

name: Intensity interferometry and quantum sensing noise
summary: Both rely on correlation measurements: Hanbury Brown–Twiss intensity correlations probe photon statistics, while sensor readout in quantum metrology is limited by shot noise and squeezing.
breaks: Intensity interferometry exploits classical thermal-light bunching, while quantum sensing gains come from nonclassical entanglement or squeezing.

name: Coherence in OCT and speckle
summary: OCT depth resolution is set by source coherence length (low-coherence interferometry), and speckle statistics govern both optical and ultrasound image texture.

name: Super-resolution and single-molecule localization
summary: Single-molecule localization microscopy (PALM/STORM) beats the diffraction limit by fitting the point-spread function of isolated emitters, linking single-molecule fluorescence to Fourier-optics resolution theory.

name: Medical imaging as Fourier optics
summary: Medical imaging modalities use transfer-function, sampling and deconvolution ideas first developed in Fourier optics.

name: Fourier imaging: lens, CT and MRI k-space
summary: A lens performs a spatial Fourier transform; MRI samples k-space directly and CT uses the Fourier slice theorem. Reconstruction is Fourier synthesis with MTF-limited resolution.

name: Image quality via MTF
summary: Modulation transfer function and noise power spectrum quantify medical image quality exactly as in optical imaging systems.

name: Beam optics as ray-transfer matrices
summary: Linear transfer matrices for quadrupoles and drifts mirror ABCD ray matrices; Twiss parameters mirror Gaussian-beam parameters and emittance mirrors etendue.

name: Interferometry in OCT
summary: OCT uses Michelson low-coherence interferometry to gate backscattered light by path length, and ultrasound beam focusing and arrays rely on the same diffraction and array-factor physics.

name: RF cavities as electromagnetic resonators
summary: Accelerating RF and SRF cavities are resonant waveguide modes; field patterns, Q factor and wall losses follow from cavity electrodynamics.

name: Absorption and dielectric response in spectroscopy
summary: Molecular absorption bands are the imaginary part of the dielectric function; Kramers–Kronig relations link absorption and refractive index.

name: Reflection and absorption of radiation
summary: Fresnel reflection and absorption set surface albedo and emissivity, and skin-depth-like penetration governs microwave remote sensing.

name: Seismic and EM wave reflection analogy
summary: Seismic P/S reflection and refraction at interfaces follows Snell's law with Zoeppritz amplitudes, paralleling Fresnel coefficients and polarization-dependent reflection.
breaks: Elastic waves have longitudinal and mode-converted components, so there are more coupled modes than the two EM polarizations.

name: MRI RF coils and field propagation
summary: MRI excitation and detection use RF coils and resonant circuits, and at high field wavelength effects in tissue produce B1 inhomogeneity governed by EM wave propagation.

name: Device electrostatics via Poisson equation
summary: The depletion region of a p-n junction and MOS gate electrostatics are Poisson boundary-value problems, solved numerically in TCAD.

name: Magnetometry and magnetization response
summary: NV-centre and atomic magnetometers and SQUIDs measure the B field of magnetized samples, so interpreting signals needs dipole fields and bound-current models.

name: Accelerator magnets from magnetostatics
summary: Dipole and quadrupole magnet design uses magnetostatic field solutions and multipole expansion of the 2D field, with pole shaping setting harmonic content.

name: Field multipoles and nonlinear beam dynamics
summary: Sextupole and higher multipole errors in magnets drive chromatic and resonant nonlinear beam motion; multipole decomposition of the field organizes these effects.

name: Silicon photonics and electronic fabrication
summary: Silicon photonic chips reuse CMOS lithography and materials platforms from semiconductor devices, merging electronic and photonic components.

name: FEL as a laser without a bound medium
summary: SASE FELs amplify radiation through collective microbunching of free electrons, analogous to gain with stimulated emission in lasers, but with no population inversion.
breaks: Gain comes from classical electron bunching, not quantized level inversion; SASE starts from shot noise, with poor temporal coherence.

name: Semiconductor diode lasers
summary: LEDs and diode lasers realize stimulated emission and population inversion in a p-n junction, with cavity feedback setting threshold and linewidth.

name: Multidimensional and nonlinear spectroscopy
summary: Coherent Raman, 2D electronic and vibrational spectroscopies are higher-order nonlinear susceptibility measurements, using pulse sequences and phase matching from nonlinear optics.

name: Attosecond X-ray FELs and HHG
summary: Attosecond pulses are produced both by high-harmonic generation and by FEL pulse-shortening schemes; they serve the same time-resolved spectroscopy of electrons.

name: Femtochemistry with ultrafast pulses
summary: Femtosecond pump-probe pulses resolve nuclear motion through transition states and conical intersections; attosecond pulses extend this to electronic dynamics.

name: Reaction dynamics probed by ultrafast optics
summary: Reaction dynamics supplies the wave-packet and potential-surface questions that ultrafast optics answers, including coherent control and conical-intersection passage.

name: Radiation theory behind light sources
summary: Synchrotron, undulator and FEL emission follow from the radiation of relativistic accelerated charges described by Liénard–Wiechert fields.
